say: Three a.m. Four hundred kilometres above Earth... the crew of the space station is fast asleep.
cap: 3 a.m. 400 km above Earth, the crew of the space station is fast asleep.

say: But who's watching over them? Wearables are uncomfortable around the clock. And cameras? Nobody wants one in their bedroom.

say: Here's the twist. The station already has Wi-Fi. Every breath, every movement, ripples through those signals. And we can read them.

say: Our AI turns those ripples into insight: tracking breathing, recognising activity, and catching danger, like a fall, or sudden stillness. No cameras. Nothing to wear.
cap: Our AI turns those ripples into insight: tracking breathing, recognising activity, and catching danger, like a fall or sudden stillness. No cameras. Nothing to wear.

say: And when something goes wrong, mission control knows in seconds, with a clear alert, and an AI briefing on every astronaut.

say: No new hardware. No lost privacy. Just smarter use of what's already on board. Spatial C.S.I. Invisible protection, for the people exploring space.
